page: Vultr vcg-a100-12c-120g-80vram is an x86_64 dedicated server instance configured primarily for high-memory and data-centric deployments. The system is powered by an Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.0 GHz, offering 12 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The platform comes equipped with 120.0 GB of system RAM, providing an abundant 10.0 GB of memory per core. Local high-speed storage is bundled via a 1400 GB NVMe solid-state drive, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Advanced CPU instruction sets, including AVX-512 extensions, are present for specialized vector computations.

Standardized benchmark testing reflects balanced mid-tier processing capabilities, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 9798.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 20434.14. Single-core throughput falls within the middle bracket, registering 1470.0 on Geekbench and 1789.58 in stress-ng evaluations. In data-handling assessments, the memory subsystem demonstrated 124.83 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations alongside Redis throughput reaching 22.96 million SET operations per second. Conversely, CPU-based machine learning inference reflects hardware boundaries, delivering 22.91 prompt tokens per second on medium 7B models.

With a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 10:1 alongside 1400 GB of fast NVMe storage, the configuration provides strong resource density for memory-bound tasks. The 2.0 GHz base frequency presents a design tradeoff for clock-sensitive single-threaded jobs, but the dedicated physical cores avoid multi-tenant noisy-neighbor disruption. Consequently, the instance is well aligned with transactional databases, in-memory caching systems, static web serving infrastructure, and ETL data processing workloads.

Across benchmark evaluations, the server achieves median-tier results, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 9798.0, a PassMark score of 20434.14, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 124.83 GB/sec.
